label: Domestic Violence
assignment: Discover confidential, survivor-centered domestic-violence resources realistically available to people in {service_area}. Investigate immediate safety, shelter, advocacy, protective orders, medical and legal support, financial stabilization, housing, and recovery without exposing survivor information. Verify current access methods, populations served, confidentiality, after-hours response, and safe contact practices.
include: Confidential hotlines, safety planning, emergency response, and shelter
Protective-order, court, immigration, victim-rights, and legal advocacy
Medical, forensic, counseling, child and family, and culturally responsive support
Transportation, phones, emergency funds, housing, employment, and relocation assistance
Services for men, LGBTQ people, immigrants, disabled survivors, teens, elders, and rural communities
exclude: Couples counseling or mediation presented as a safety response where abuse or coercive control is present
Public-facing contact details that could compromise a confidential shelter location
Generic crime-victim information without a reachable domestic-violence service
verificationQuestions: What is the safest current contact method and is help available after hours?
Are shelter location and survivor information kept confidential?
Which genders, ages, family arrangements, immigration statuses, and service areas are served?
Can an advocate help with protection, transport, children, pets, housing, and legal needs?

stages.title: Immediate safety and confidential access
stages.instruction: Investigate confidential hotlines, safety planning, emergency shelter, transportation, pet safety, medical response, and after-hours access. Do not expose confidential locations or recommend unsafe contact practices.

stages.title: Legal and systems advocacy
stages.instruction: Investigate protective orders, court advocacy, victim rights, immigration relief, law-enforcement accompaniment, forensic and medical advocacy, and help navigating benefits and documentation.

stages.title: Stabilization and recovery
stages.instruction: Investigate counseling, child and family services, phones, emergency funds, employment, housing, relocation, and culturally responsive services for diverse survivors.

stages.title: Safety and population gap review
stages.instruction: Cross-check confidentiality, capacity, eligibility, service-area boundaries, accessibility, language, gender and age inclusion, pet and child options, and safe handoffs. Identify populations or hours without a realistic response.
